newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 19.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Wednesday:
* On Tuesday, the Dow Jones industrial average ended up 78.50 points at 7,067.46 as blue-chip stocks surged to another record high amid a spate of mergers and as the dollar remained strong.
* Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad told parliament on Tuesday the Indonesian government's outstanding foreign debt stood at $54.6 billion on November 30, 1996.
* Media reports that the health of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping was deteriorating seen dampening sentiment, brokers said.
* On Tuesday, the Jakarta Composite Index closed 6.55 points lower at 695.22 points on continued profit taking in several blue chips.
* On Wednesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,387.70/8.70 in early trading against the opening of 2,385.75/86.75.

* State-controlled tin miner Tambang Timah on Tuesday's government announcement that state companies would only be allowed to participate in the huge Busang gold project when it enters the production stage.
* Country's largest car maker Astra International on its shareholders' meeting on Wednesday to get approval for a change in its board of commissioners.

* Lippo Life on a report in the Bisnis Indonesia newspaper that the capital market supervisory agency Bapepam had rejected the company's proposal to a rights issue because it was not in line with its prospectus.
* Indonesian salt producer PT Fiskaragung Perkasa on its announcement that the firm had revised up its 1997 net profit forecast to 144 billion rupiah from 104.1 billion rupiah.
* Alumunium products maker PT Prima Alloy Steel on its proposed stock split and bonus share issue at its extraordinary shareholders meeting on March 27.
* Anwar Sierad on its announcement of a stock split and changes to the board of directors, which are subject to shareholders' approval at a meeting on February 28.
